items.followUp: Define electron affinity and state its general trend down a group.

rubric.why: The definition must identify the energy needed to remove an electron from a gaseous atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that energy is required to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom.

rubric.why: Ionization energy generally decreases down a group as atomic size and shielding increase.
rubric.description: Gives the trend down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ionization energy decreases down a group.

modelAnswer: Ionization energy is the energy required to remove the outermost electron from an isolated gaseous atom.
It generally decreases down a group because atomic size and shielding increase.

items.followUp: Why does atomic size generally increase down a group?

rubric.why: Metals contain electrons that are free to move through the solid.
rubric.description: Identifies the mobile electrons in metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that metals have free, mobile, or delocalized electrons.

rubric.why: The movement of these electrons transfers electrical charge.
rubric.description: Explains how the electrons conduct electricity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the movement or flow of electrons to electrical conduction.

modelAnswer: Metals contain free, mobile electrons that can move through the solid.
These electrons carry electrical charge, so metals conduct electricity.

items.followUp: What type of bond is formed in a hydrogen molecule, and how many electron pairs are shared?

rubric.why: The nitrogen molecule contains a triple bond.
rubric.description: Identifies the bond as a triple bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the bond in nitrogen is a triple bond.

rubric.why: Each nitrogen atom shares three electrons, forming three shared pairs in a covalent bond.
rubric.description: Identifies the bond as covalent and explains electron sharing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that nitrogen atoms share three pairs of electrons or form a covalent bond by sharing electrons.

modelAnswer: Each nitrogen atom shares three electrons with the other nitrogen atom.
The atoms form a triple covalent bond, written N≡N.

items.followUp: Define diffusion and give one example from everyday life.

rubric.why: Diffusion is the movement or spreading of particles from a region of higher concentration to one of lower concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing particle movement from higher to lower concentration.

rubric.why: A suitable example demonstrates particles spreading through another substance or space.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example, such as the smell of perfume spreading through a room.

modelAnswer: Diffusion is the movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
For example, the smell of perfume spreads through a room by diffusion.

items.followUp: Why does a solution form a homogeneous mixture while a suspension does not?

rubric.why: Suspended particles remain separate rather than dissolving uniformly in the medium.
rubric.description: Explains the state of suspension particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the particles remain undissolved or are large dispersed particles.

rubric.why: The particles are not uniformly distributed throughout the mixture and may settle, so the mixture is heterogeneous.
rubric.description: Explains why the mixture is not homogeneous.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking uneven distribution or settling to the mixture being non-uniform.

modelAnswer: The particles of a suspension do not dissolve uniformly in the medium.
They are unevenly distributed and may settle, so the suspension is a heterogeneous, not homogeneous, mixture.

items.followUp: Why does potassium have a lower ionization energy than sodium?

rubric.why: Sodium has a smaller atomic radius than potassium because potassium has an additional electron shell.
rubric.description: Compares the atomic sizes of sodium and potassium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that sodium is smaller than potassium, or that potassium has an extra shell.

rubric.why: Sodium's outer electron is more strongly attracted to the nucleus and therefore requires more energy to remove.
rubric.description: Links size and attraction to ionization energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that sodium's outer electron is held more strongly and takes more energy to remove.

modelAnswer: A sodium atom is smaller than a potassium atom; potassium has an additional electron shell.
Sodium's outer electron is closer to the nucleus and more strongly attracted, so more energy is needed to remove it.

items.followUp: Why are noble gases generally unreactive?

rubric.why: Silver and gold have a low tendency to lose electrons, so they do not react readily.
rubric.description: States their low tendency to lose electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that silver and gold do not readily lose electrons.

rubric.why: Their electrons are relatively difficult to remove, which is associated with their low reactivity.
rubric.description: Gives a supporting reason for their low reactivity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking their low reactivity to high ionization energy or a stable electron arrangement.

modelAnswer: Silver and gold have a low tendency to lose electrons.
Their electrons are relatively difficult to remove, so these metals are among the least reactive.

items.followUp: Write any five properties of cathode rays.

rubric.why: Canal rays consist of positively charged particles.
rubric.description: States the positive charge of canal rays.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying canal rays as positively charged.

rubric.why: Canal rays travel in straight lines.
rubric.description: States that canal rays travel in straight lines.

rubric.why: Their deflection in an electric field is toward the negative plate, opposite to cathode rays.
rubric.description: States how canal rays are deflected.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing their electric-field deflection or that it is opposite to cathode rays.

rubric.why: Canal rays are positive ions formed from the gas in the discharge tube.
rubric.description: Identifies the particles in canal rays as gas ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they consist of positive ions of the gas in the tube.

rubric.why: The charge-to-mass ratio of canal-ray particles varies with the gas used in the tube.
rubric.description: States that their charge-to-mass ratio depends on the gas.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the ratio varies with the gas used.

modelAnswer: Canal rays are streams of positively charged particles.
In an electric field, they are deflected toward the negative plate, opposite to cathode rays.
They consist of positive ions formed from the gas in the discharge tube.
Their charge-to-mass ratio depends on the nature of the gas in the tube.
